def save_lineplot(x, y, xlabel, ylabel, title, fname):
    sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
    plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
    plt.plot(x, y, marker="o")
    for _x, _y in zip(x, y):
        plt.text(_x, _y, f"{_y:.2f}")
    plt.xlabel(xlabel)
    plt.ylabel(ylabel)
    plt.title(title)
    plt.legend([title])
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(fname, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close()
    print(f"Figure saved: {fname}")


def save_barplot(names, values, ylabel, title, fname):
    sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
    plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
    ax = sns.barplot(x=names, y=values, palette="crest")
    for p, v in zip(ax.patches, values):
        ax.annotate(f"{v:.2f}", (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., v), ha='center', va='baseline')
    plt.ylabel(ylabel)
    plt.title(title)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(fname, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close()
    print(f"Figure saved: {fname}")


# -----------------------------------------
# EXPERIMENT 1  –  Full SD-1.5 training
# -----------------------------------------

class Experiment1:
    def __init__(self, args):
        self.args = args
        self.device = torch.device("cuda:0")
        set_seed(args.seed)
        pynvml.nvmlInit()

    # --------------------------------------------------
    # Build model, optimizer, schedulers
    # --------------------------------------------------
    def _build_model(self, baseline: bool):
        print("\nLoading Stable-Diffusion-1.5 UNet … baseline=", baseline)
        unet = UNet2DConditionModel.from_pretrained(
            "runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5", subfolder="unet"
        )
        if not baseline:
            unet = make_rechunked(
                unet,
                rev=True,
                chunk_hw=4,
                chunk_tb=2,
                flash_attn=True,
                gated=True,
            )
        unet = unet.half().to(self.device)
        return unet

    def _optimizer(self, model):
        optim_cls = diffusers.optimization.AdamW8bit if self.args.use_nf4 else torch.optim.AdamW
        optim = optim_cls(
            model.parameters(),
            lr=1e-4,
            betas=(0.9, 0.95),
            weight_decay=0.05,
        )
        return optim

    # --------------------------------------------------
    def run(self):
        print("=" * 80)
        print("EXPERIMENT 1  –  Full Stable-Diffusion-1.5 training under 16 GB")
        print("Goal  : show ReChuNet trains end-to-end where vanilla OOMs")
        print("Design: baseline vs rechunet, 3 seeds, log memory ± stats …")
        print("=" * 80)

        tokenizer = transformers.CLIPTokenizer.from_pretrained("openai/clip-vit-large-patch14")
        dataset = LaionDataset(self.args.laion_shards, tokenizer)
        loader = dataset.loader(batch_size=4, num_workers=8)
        noise_scheduler = DDPMScheduler(num_train_timesteps=1000)

        results = defaultdict(list)  # collect across seeds

        for variant in ("baseline", "rechunet"):
            for seed in self.args.seeds:
                set_seed(seed)
                model = self._build_model(baseline=(variant == "baseline"))

                try:
                    optim = self._optimizer(model)
                    scaler = torch.cuda.amp.GradScaler(enabled=False)  # fp16 already
                    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
                    mem_peak = 0
                    step_times: List[float] = []
                    iterator = tqdm(enumerate(loader), total=self.args.max_steps, desc=f"{variant}-{seed}")
                    for step, batch in iterator:
                        if step >= self.args.max_steps:
                            break
                        t0 = time.time()
                        loss = diffusion_step(model, noise_scheduler, batch, self.device)
                        loss.backward()
                        if (step + 1) % 2 == 0:
                            optim.step(); optim.zero_grad()
                        torch.cuda.synchronize()
                        step_times.append(time.time() - t0)
                        mem_peak = max(mem_peak, cuda_memory_mb())
                    mem_nvml = nvml_memory_mb()
                except RuntimeError as e:  # OOM
                    print(f"{variant} seed {seed} OOM → recording failure")
                    mem_peak = math.nan
                    step_times = [math.nan]

                # --- log
                results["variant"].append(variant)
                results["seed"].append(seed)
                results["peak_mem_mb"].append(mem_peak)
                results["iter_per_sec"].append(1 / np.nanmean(step_times))

                # free GPU for next run
                del model, optim
                torch.cuda.empty_cache()

        df = pd.DataFrame(results)
        print("\nNumerical results (per-seed):")
        print(df)

        # aggregate
        agg = df.groupby("variant").agg({
            "peak_mem_mb": ["mean", "std"],
            "iter_per_sec": ["mean", "std"],
        })
        print("\nAggregate results (mean ± s.d.):\n", agg)

        # paired t-test on speed (ignore NaN rows)
        base_speed = df[df.variant == "baseline"]["iter_per_sec"].values
        rech_speed = df[df.variant == "rechunet"]["iter_per_sec"].values
        mask = ~np.isnan(base_speed) & ~np.isnan(rech_speed)
        if mask.sum() >= 2:
            t, p = stats.ttest_rel(base_speed[mask], rech_speed[mask])
            print(f"Paired t-test speed baseline vs rechunet:  t={t:.3f},  p={p:.4f}")
        else:
            print("t-test skipped (baseline OOM on ≥2 seeds)")

        # -------- figures
        fig_dir = ensure_dir("figures")
        mean_mem = df.groupby("variant")["peak_mem_mb"].mean()
        save_barplot(mean_mem.index.tolist(), mean_mem.values.tolist(),
                     ylabel="Peak memory (MB)",
                     title="Peak GPU memory – Experiment 1",
                     fname=fig_dir / "peak_memory_sd15.pdf")

        mean_speed = df.groupby("variant")["iter_per_sec"].mean()
        save_barplot(mean_speed.index.tolist(), mean_speed.values.tolist(),
                     ylabel="Iterations / sec", title="Throughput – Experiment 1",
                     fname=fig_dir / "throughput_sd15.pdf")

        print("Figures generated: peak_memory_sd15.pdf  |  throughput_sd15.pdf")
        print("Experiment 1 completed.\n")


# -----------------------------------------
# EXPERIMENT 2  –  ImageNet-256 ablation
# -----------------------------------------

class Experiment2:
    VARIANTS = {
        "A": dict(rev=False),
        "B": dict(rev=True, chunk=None, flash=False, gated=False, nf4=False),
        "C": dict(rev=True, chunk=(4, 2), flash=False, gated=False, nf4=False),
        "D": dict(rev=True, chunk=(4, 2), flash=True, gated=False, nf4=False),
        "E": dict(rev=True, chunk=(4, 2), flash=True, gated=True, nf4=False),
        "F": dict(rev=True, chunk=(4, 2), flash=True, gated=True, nf4=True),
    }

    def __init__(self, args):
        self.args = args
        self.device = torch.device("cuda:0")
        set_seed(args.seed)
        pynvml.nvmlInit()

    def _imagenet_loader(self):
        # Use torchvision for ImageNet – path must be provided
        from torchvision import datasets, transforms as T
        tr = T.Compose([
            T.RandomResizedCrop(256, interpolation=T.InterpolationMode.BICUBIC),
            T.RandomHorizontalFlip(),
            T.ToTensor(),
            T.Normalize([0.5], [0.5]),
        ])
        ds = datasets.ImageFolder(self.args.imagenet_root, transform=tr)
        loader = DataLoader(ds, batch_size=8, shuffle=True, num_workers=8, pin_memory=True)
        return loader

    def _model_for_variant(self, variant_key: str):
        cfg = self.VARIANTS[variant_key]
        m = UNet2DConditionModel.from_pretrained("runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5", subfolder="unet")
        if cfg["rev"]:
            m = make_rechunked(
                m,
                rev=True,
                chunk_hw=cfg["chunk"][0] if cfg["chunk"] else None,
                chunk_tb=cfg["chunk"][1] if cfg["chunk"] else None,
                flash_attn=cfg["flash"],
                gated=cfg["gated"],
            )
        m = m.half().to(self.device)
        return m, cfg["nf4"]

    def run(self):
        print("=" * 80)
        print("EXPERIMENT 2  –  ImageNet-256 ablation study")
        print("=" * 80)

        tokenizer = transformers.CLIPTokenizer.from_pretrained("openai/clip-vit-large-patch14")
        loader = self._imagenet_loader()
        noise_scheduler = DDPMScheduler(num_train_timesteps=1000)

        records = []
        for variant in self.VARIANTS:
            for seed in self.args.seeds:
                set_seed(seed)
                model, use_nf4 = self._model_for_variant(variant)
                optim_cls = diffusers.optimization.AdamW8bit if use_nf4 else torch.optim.AdamW
                optim = optim_cls(model.parameters(), lr=2e-4, betas=(0.9, 0.95), weight_decay=0.05)

                torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
                step_times, losses = [], []
                for step, (imgs, labels) in tqdm(enumerate(loader), total=self.args.max_steps, desc=f"{variant}-{seed}"):
                    if step >= self.args.max_steps:
                        break
                    batch = {
                        "pixel_values": imgs.to(self.device),
                        "input_ids": tokenizer([f"a photo of a {loader.dataset.classes[int(l)]}" for l in labels], padding="max_length", max_length=77, return_tensors="pt").input_ids.to(self.device),
                    }
                    t0 = time.time()
                    loss = diffusion_step(model, noise_scheduler, batch, self.device)
                    loss.backward()
                    if (step + 1) % 4 == 0:
                        optim.step(); optim.zero_grad()
                    torch.cuda.synchronize()
                    step_times.append(time.time() - t0)
                    losses.append(loss.item())

                rec = {
                    "variant": variant,
                    "seed": seed,
                    "peak_mem_mb": cuda_memory_mb(),
                    "iter_per_sec": 1 / np.mean(step_times),
                    "loss_last": np.mean(losses[-100:]),
                }
                records.append(rec)
                del model, optim
                torch.cuda.empty_cache()

        df = pd.DataFrame(records)
        print("\nPer-seed results:\n", df)
        agg = df.groupby("variant").agg(["mean", "std"])
        print("\nAggregate (mean ± s.d.):\n", agg[[("peak_mem_mb", "mean"), ("iter_per_sec", "mean")]])

        # one-way ANOVA on memory
        mem_groups = [df[df.variant == k]["peak_mem_mb"].values for k in self.VARIANTS]
        f_mem, p_mem = stats.f_oneway(*mem_groups)
        print(f"ANOVA peak-mem  F={f_mem:.2f},  p={p_mem:.4g}")

        # ------------- figures
        fig_dir = ensure_dir("figures")
        mean_mem = df.groupby("variant")["peak_mem_mb"].mean()
        save_barplot(mean_mem.index.tolist(), mean_mem.values.tolist(),
                     ylabel="Peak memory (MB)", title="Ablation – peak memory",
                     fname=fig_dir / "peak_memory_ablation.pdf")

        mean_speed = df.groupby("variant")["iter_per_sec"].mean()
        save_barplot(mean_speed.index.tolist(), mean_speed.values.tolist(),
                     ylabel="Iterations / sec", title="Ablation – speed",
                     fname=fig_dir / "throughput_ablation.pdf")

        print("Figures generated: peak_memory_ablation.pdf  |  throughput_ablation.pdf")
        print("Experiment 2 completed.\n")


# -----------------------------------------
# EXPERIMENT 3  –  2 GB DreamBooth fine-tuning
# -----------------------------------------

class Experiment3:
    def __init__(self, args):
        self.args = args
        os.environ["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = "0"
        torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction(0.15)
        self.device = torch.device("cuda:0")
        pynvml.nvmlInit()

    def _load_subject_imgs(self, subject_dir: pathlib.Path):
        from torchvision import transforms as T
        from PIL import Image
        tf = T.Compose([
            T.Resize(512, interpolation=T.InterpolationMode.BICUBIC),
            T.CenterCrop(512),
            T.ToTensor(),
            T.Normalize([0.5], [0.5]),
        ])
        imgs = []
        for p in subject_dir.glob("*.jpg"):
            imgs.append(tf(Image.open(p).convert("RGB")))
        return torch.stack(imgs)

    def _model(self, baseline: str):
        unet = UNet2DConditionModel.from_pretrained("runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5", subfolder="unet")
        if baseline == "rechunet":
            unet = make_rechunked(unet, rev=True, chunk_hw=4, chunk_tb=2, flash_attn=True, gated=True)
        elif baseline == "hollowed":
            from hollowed_net import apply_hollow  # external lib
            unet = apply_hollow(unet, hollow_ratio=0.39)
        unet = unet.half().to(self.device)
        return unet

    def run(self):
        print("=" * 80)
        print("EXPERIMENT 3  –  DreamBooth under 2 GB budget")
        print("=" * 80)

        root = pathlib.Path(self.args.dreambooth_root)
        subjects = [p for p in root.iterdir() if p.is_dir()][:10]
        tokenizer = transformers.CLIPTokenizer.from_pretrained("openai/clip-vit-large-patch14")
        noise_scheduler = DDPMScheduler(num_train_timesteps=1000)

        methods = ["baseline", "hollowed", "rechunet"]
        summary = []
        for method in methods:
            fits_gpu = True
            try:
                torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
                for subj in subjects:
                    imgs = self._load_subject_imgs(subj).to(self.device)
                    prompts = [f"a photo of {subj.name}"] * len(imgs)
                    input_ids = tokenizer(prompts, padding="max_length", max_length=77, return_tensors="pt").input_ids.to(self.device)
                    model = self._model(method)
                    optim = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=5e-6)

                    for step in range(800):
                        idx = step % len(imgs)
                        batch = {
                            "pixel_values": imgs[idx : idx + 1],
                            "input_ids": input_ids[idx : idx + 1],
                        }
                        loss = diffusion_step(model, noise_scheduler, batch, self.device)
                        loss.backward()
                        if (step + 1) % 4 == 0:
                            optim.step(); optim.zero_grad()
                mem_peak = cuda_memory_mb()
            except RuntimeError as e:
                if "out of memory" in str(e).lower():
                    fits_gpu = False
                    mem_peak = math.nan
                else:
                    raise

            summary.append({"method": method, "fits": fits_gpu, "peak_mem_mb": mem_peak})
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()

        df = pd.DataFrame(summary)
        print("\nSummary:\n", df)

        fig_dir = ensure_dir("figures")
        save_barplot(df.method.tolist(), df.peak_mem_mb.fillna(0).tolist(),
                     ylabel="Peak memory (MB)", title="DreamBooth – memory usage",
                     fname=fig_dir / "peak_memory_dreambooth.pdf")
        print("Figure generated: peak_memory_dreambooth.pdf")
        print("Experiment 3 completed.\n")


# -----------------------------------------
# main CLI
# -----------------------------------------

def parse_args():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--exp", type=int, choices=[1, 2, 3], required=True)
    p.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=13)
    p.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, nargs="*", default=[13, 17, 23])

    # exp1 specific
    p.add_argument("--laion_shards", type=str, help="webdataset shards pattern", default="/path/to/shards/{000000..000100}.tar")
    p.add_argument("--max_steps", type=int, default=200)  # shorten for demo; set 200000 in real run
    p.add_argument("--use_nf4", action="store_true")

    # exp2 specific
    p.add_argument("--imagenet_root", type=str, default="/path/to/imagenet/train")

    # exp3 specific
    p.add_argument("--dreambooth_root", type=str, default="/path/to/subjects")

    return p.parse_args()


def main():
    args = parse_args()
    if args.exp == 1:
        Experiment1(args).run()
    elif args.exp == 2:
        Experiment2(args).run()
    elif args.exp == 3:
        Experiment3(args).run()
    else:
        raise ValueError


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

experimental_analysis.analysis_report:
Summary of provided outputs
1. Installation phase: All required Python packages (PyTorch 2.8, diffusers, etc.) were installed successfully, so the software stack is intact.

2. Runtime configuration that was actually executed
   • batch_size          : 8
   • image_size          : 64 (far below the 256–512 advertised in the paper)
   • num_steps           : 500 (vs. ≥200k in the plan)
   • use_rechunet        : 0  → the standard UNet was trained, not ReChuNet
   • chunk_hw / chunk_tb : 2,2  (has no effect because ReChuNet wrapper was disabled)
   • Dataset             : “Falling back to synthetic random images ✨”  → no real LAION, ImageNet or DreamBooth data were used.
   • Device              : CUDA, peak memory 98 MB

3. Observed results
   • Peak GPU memory     : 98 MB (orders of magnitude smaller than any realistic diffusion‐training workload)
   • Loss curve & model  : Saved, but only for a tiny toy UNet on random noise.
   • No FID / CLIP-score, no throughput numbers, no statistical tests.

Comparison with the proposed experimental plan
• None of the three planned experiments (full SD-1.5, ImageNet-256 ablation, 2 GB DreamBooth) were executed.
• The code fell back to its synthetic “smoke-test” path, which deliberately bypasses every memory-intensive component.
• ReChuNet was never enabled, so there is no measurement whatsoever for the new method.
• Consequently, there are no baselines, no seeds, no variance estimates and no significance tests.

Does the new method show a clear advantage?
No. The run that was actually carried out does not use ReChuNet and does not correspond to any realistic diffusion workload, therefore:
• Memory usage (98 MB) cannot be compared to the 16 GB baseline claim.
• Speed and quality metrics are absent.
• The results neither confirm nor deny the claims in the paper—they are simply irrelevant.

Conclusion
The supplied “Experimental results” do not validate ReChuNet at all; they only prove that the minimal smoke-test script can train a tiny UNet on random data inside 98 MB. No evidence has been produced that ReChuNet enables 3–7× memory savings, maintains quality, or supports on-device fine-tuning as claimed. Additional, correctly configured experiments must be run before any advantage can be asserted.

consistency_feedback:
Major inconsistencies prevent the current results from supporting the paper’s central claims.

1. Results are largely hypothetical.  Nearly all numbers in the manuscript are labelled “expected”.  The only actually-executed run visible in the log trained a *vanilla* UNet on `torchvision.FakeData` for 200 mini-steps and used a dummy loss.  No real LAION, ImageNet or DreamBooth experiments were run, so none of the headline memory (≤7 GB on SD-1.5, ≤1.6 GB on SD-XL) or quality (±0.2 FID, human A/B 68 %) figures are demonstrated.

2. Critical components absent at run time.  The log shows “rechuwrapper not found – falling back to vanilla UNet”, so none of the five proposed techniques (reversible blocks, chunking, etc.) were active.  Observed peak RAM ≈9 GB therefore cannot validate the claimed 4–7× reduction.

3. Statistical analysis missing.  The manuscript promises averages ± s.d. over three seeds and binomial tests for human studies, but no p-values, confidence intervals or variance numbers are supplied.  Human preference rates and FID/CLIP deltas are asserted without evidence.

4. Internal contradictions.
   • Table in Exp-1 claims baseline peak RAM 14.6 GB under a 12 GB cap – impossible.
   • Expected throughput says ReChuNet is 1.21 it/s (≈baseline/0.75) yet also “overall 1.3× slower than baseline”.
   • Quality claims “no degradation” and simultaneously “FID 15.0 vs 14.9 (baseline)”, which is within noise but still contradicts the earlier claim that Hollowed-Net was +1.4 FID worse – no real data backs either.

5. Place-holders and dummy code.
   • Data loaders use `FakeData`; DreamBooth loss is `(images**2).mean()`.
   • Metrics such as FID are never computed; `quality = –0.322` in the log is unexplained.

6. Reproducibility obstacles.  Key package `rechuwrapper` and `hollowed_net` are absent; therefore readers cannot reproduce the intended experiments.

Recommendations for improvement:
• Run the full training/fine-tuning experiments on the stated datasets with the actual ReChuNet implementation enabled.
• Report real memory traces, throughput and quality metrics for at least three independent seeds; include means, standard deviations and exact p-values for human studies.
• Provide ablation tables with real measurements, not expectations.
• Ensure baseline fits the enforced memory cap or explain deviations.
• Release `rechuwrapper` and scripts that download the real datasets so others can replicate the study.
• Replace dummy losses and FakeData with the genuine diffusion objectives and data.
The manuscript is almost entirely a *research plan* rather than a presentation of completed experiments. 

1. Missing real results.
   • All key tables (peak-memory, FID, CLIP, human A/B, ANOVA, t-tests) are filled with the words “Expected Demonstration” or placeholder numbers.  
   • The only concrete log included in the "Experimental Results" section is a toy run that trains for 500 steps on synthetic random images, reaches 98 MB peak memory, and never touches LAION, ImageNet or DreamBooth.  This log cannot substantiate any of the central claims (3-7× memory reduction, ±0.2 FID parity, human preference ≥68 %, etc.).

2. Internal contradictions and control issues.
   • The plan promises three seeds for every variant, yet the toy run is single-seed.
   • The global hardware narrative targets a single 16 GB Tesla T4, but the methods section also quotes runs on RTX-3060, 4090 and A100.  No rationale or cross-device variance analysis is supplied.
   • DreamBooth is said to run under a 2 GB cap on the same T4 via `set_per_process_memory_fraction(0.15)`.  This is *not* equivalent to a device with 2 GB physical VRAM; kernel residency, page-fault latency and driver over-commit make the measurement incomparable.

3. Statistical analysis absent.
   • p-values, confidence intervals and ANOVA tests are only outlined; no numerical outputs are shown.  
   • No raw FID / IS distributions, variance across seeds, or effect sizes are reported, so significance of the claimed ±0.2 FID cannot be verified.

4. Reproducibility gap.
   • Although extensive code stubs are listed, they still fall back to "synthetic random images ✨" when real data is unavailable, violating the stated “real datasets only” rule.
   • The critical `rechuwrapper` package is referenced but never imported in the toy run, so none of the reversible or chunked logic is actually exercised.

5. Unsupported conclusions.
   • Because the evidence is missing, none of the headline conclusions—full SD-1.5 training in 7 GB, <35 % slowdown, on-device DreamBooth—are experimentally demonstrated.

Recommendations for improvement
   a. Run the three experiments as written, capture real metrics, and include the raw CSV/plots in the paper.
   b. Report exact p-values, CIs and effect sizes; show seed-level scatter plots to visualise variance.
   c. Verify that `make_rechunked()` is active by printing model graphs or parameter names.
   d. Use a genuine 2 GB-VRAM device (e.g. RTX A2000 4 GB with half memory reserved) or a cloud GPU with enforced MIG slice to validate the 2 GB claim.
   e. Remove “expected” language; replace with measured numbers.
The manuscript lays out an ambitious, carefully-thought experimental plan (three large–scale studies, real datasets, multiple seeds, statistical tests, ablations).  However, the **only concrete results provided** are the build log and a single 500-step toy run that:
• Uses “synthetic random images ✨” instead of LAION, ImageNet or DreamBooth data.
• Trains a tiny 64×64 network for ~9 s, peaking at just 98 MB of GPU memory.
• Reports no FID, CLIP, human preference, p-values, ANOVA, or confidence intervals.
• Includes no comparison to a baseline UNet or to the proposed ReChuNet (use_rechunet=0).  Therefore the core claims—3-7× memory reduction, ≤0.2 FID difference, successful DreamBooth under 2 GB—are untested.
• Only one seed, no variance estimates, no statistical validity.

This is a severe mismatch between the promised methodology and the evidence actually produced; none of the stated hypotheses are evaluated.  Consequently the results cannot support any scientific claims at this stage.

Key recommendations to achieve internal consistency:
1. Run the experiments exactly as described: real LAION-512, ImageNet-256 and DreamBooth datasets; three seeds per condition; collect peak-memory, FID/IS/CLIP, throughput.  Release raw CSV logs.
2. Present complete baseline vs ReChuNet tables with means ± s.d.  Perform the planned paired t-tests, ANOVA, Tukey and binomial analyses; include p-values and effect sizes.
3. Show training curves and sample images to demonstrate qualitative parity.
4. Verify that the code does not silently fall back to synthetic data (add CI check that real shards are loaded; abort on missing datasets).
5. Include reproducibility artifacts: commit hash, environment file, and instructions that reproduce the full runs.
6. If full LAION training is too costly, down-scale but keep the same comparative structure (e.g., LAION-subset 1 M images, 50 k steps) and report how scaling affects metrics.

Until such evidence is provided, the experimental section is internally inconsistent with its claims.
